messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime p99 latency breach on /v1/generate detected in us-west-2 (p99 5800ms, threshold 2500ms). Alert rule: realtime_p99_regression_v2. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/alerts/3998765432 :rotating_light:
oncall-sre: I’m on it. paging now. starting quick triage — linking traces and logs.
oncall-sre: Quick checks: 1) recent deploy? 2) traffic spike? 3) backend errors? 4) streaming stalls?
alice: I can check deploys and rollout status. hitting deploy history... nothing in last 45m.
carla: Looking at traffic — 2x spike in avg req/s for realtime-proxy over the last 10m. No config changes.
derek: Traces: a lot of tails show long backend wait at runtime-worker v3.8, class="kv-cache-miss" appears often.
eva: I'm pulling live flamegraphs and tail histograms now. If KV cache on these routes is cold it would explain p99s.
infra-bot: Autoscale event: pool-rt-gpu scaled from 12 -> 18 pods 6m ago due to CPU pressure. No failures in node provisioning.
oncall-sre: Good. can someone run a quick query for model-serving latency vs network egress? also check queue lengths on the request proxy.
alice: Querying logs: proxy queue depth spiked to 420 at 16:12:42 UTC, baseline 30. Many 429 retries from internal clients.
carla: Internal rate limit bumping? I see a recent config change to batching window on the router 30m ago (batch_ms=12 -> 40). Could be increasing queuing for large bursts.
derek: Sample trace: ```
span: proxy_enqueue -> 2.8s
span: proxy_dispatch -> 0.1s
span: worker_kv_lookup -> 2.5s
span: model_generate -> 0.2s
```
eva: That worker_kv_lookup looks suspicious. hitting backend kv store from runtime-worker shows elevated latency (876ms P99). Could be KVS throttle during spike.
oncall-sre: Actionable mitigations: A) temporarily revert batching window to 12ms on router to reduce queueing B) enable fallback routing to smaller model variant or idle pool C) add circuit-breaker to drop long-queued requests D) throttle internal non-critical background jobs. Which is lowest-risk first?
alice: Reverting batch window is quick, low risk. I can push a config rollback to router 1 (canary) and observe.
carla: I'll prepare fallback routing policy to route > 3s in-queue requests to dedicated-small model variant (lower cost/higher latency tolerance) — need approval to enable.
derek: I'll open a KV incident with infra team, but for immediate relief can we enable a warm-KV prefetch for hot keys? That is a code change though.
eva: Warm prefetch requires a minor runtime change; not immediate. Prefer config-level mitigations now.
oncall-sre: OK do rollback first. alice, proceed with canary. I'll monitor p99 and queue depth.
alice: Rolling back batch_ms -> 12 on router-canary now. command: ```curl -X POST https://ops.redwood/api/configs/router-canary -d '{"batch_ms":12}'```
alice: done, canary applied to 2/20 routers. watching metrics...
carla: Preparing fallback policy in case rollback not sufficient. draft policy: route requests with queue_time > 1500ms OR proxy_retry_count > 1 -> model: rtd-small-v1. Need oncall-sre ack to flip.
oncall-sre: Ack, standby to flip after canary results. Also enable temporary internal rate limit for background jobs: set background-service-limit=30% of capacity. carla/derek you take action?
derek: I'll patch the background job limiter now. command: `kubectl set env deploy/bg-workers MAX_CONCURRENCY=30`
derek: done. infra-bot: noted scaling events remain stable.
carla: Canary metrics: p99 on canary routers dropped from 5800ms -> 2900ms in first 60s. Queue depth on those routers down to ~90.
oncall-sre: Good sign. Continue canary ramp to 6/20. If p99 <= 3s across canary after 2m, roll to 100%.
alice: Ramp to 6/20 applied. monitoring.
product-ops: Heads-up — customer X reported degraded interactive experience, CS queued a ticket. I'll update them with mitigation steps.
carla: Canary p99 stable at 2700ms, overall cluster p99 down to 3600ms (still above SLO). plan: full rollback of batch_ms across routers and enable fallback policy as a safety net.
oncall-sre: Proceed. alice roll full config, carla prepare feature flip for fallback route but hold until after full rollback completes.
alice: Rolling full rollback now. estimated 1m to propagate.
alice: Full rollback complete. cluster p99 now 1900ms, below SLO. Queue depths normalizing.
derek: Background job limiter engaged, KV store P99 still elevated but load reduced so should recover.
eva: Starting a follow-up runbook: 1) postmortem checklist 2) add alert for queue depth > 200 3) add KV throttling metric 4) evaluate batch window defaults vs traffic patterns 5) evaluate hot-key prefetch triggers.
oncall-sre: Great. I'll close the immediate page. Moving to post-incident channel for RCA. Assign owners: KV perf — derek, router batching config — alice, fallback routing policy docs — carla, customer comms — product-ops.
product-ops: I'll send customer update and thank you note.
incident-bot: Incident action: page resolved. Incident severity: SEV3. Start RCA draft: https://docs.redwood/incidents/3998765432-rca
oncall-sre: Thanks team. We'll add a short live mitigation playbook for sudden traffic bursts and update the alert to include queue depth and kv latency correlation. Closing thread in 30m unless anyone objects. :thumbsup:
